title: Broken economics of the antibiotic R&D pipeline
bottleneck: WHO's 2025 analysis found the clinical antibacterial pipeline shrank from 97 candidates in 2023 to 90 in 2025, with only 15 qualifying as innovative and just 5 active against critical-priority pathogens. Since 2017, only 17 new agents reached market, and only two represent new chemical classes.
why_it_blocks: Antimicrobial resistance is associated with nearly 5 million deaths annually; a pipeline this thin cannot outpace evolving resistance.
current_state: The market is fundamentally broken: new antibiotics must be used sparingly to preserve effectiveness, destroying returns, so large pharmaceutical companies have exited and 90% of preclinical work sits with fragile small firms. WHO calls for innovation-focused incentives and a stable pipeline. Pull incentives such as subscription-style payments are being piloted in a few countries, but nothing yet operates at the scale the crisis demands.
